thread:
incident-bot: PagerDuty P1 — production-inference: sustained 5xx spike detected (420/min). Routing to @sre-oncall-jamie.

sre-oncall-jamie: seeing it, joining. quick triage: are error types mostly 503 from model binary or network timeouts?

matt: 503s with downstream kvstore timeouts, but there's also a small bump in OOM logs on a subset of pods. digging.

priya: I can spin a temporary routing rule to fallback-quantized-model group to reduce user impact if you want me to. that should lower latency and abort some retry storms.

olivia: customer-impact: only hosted API traffic to eu-west-1 appears to hit it so far. product-ops confirms a few unhappy customers pinged support.

incident-bot: Note — deploy-bot started canary rollback for inference-service at 00:12 UTC per auto-rollback policy.

infra-bot: temporary sqash rule applied: alerts tagged production-inference severity=page -> dedupe-window=5m, max-rate=10/min for the group. visible in routing-config: /infra/pd-routes.

sre-oncall-jamie: mitigation: 1) rollback canary in progress 2) apply temporary PD ratecap (infra-bot) 3) route ~20% traffic to fallback-quantized-model (priya) 4) live metrics dashboards pinned to team so we can watch noisiness.

matt: logs: main stack trace shows `kvstore.ReadTimeout` at ~250ms. We briefly saturated a connection pool because of a slow downstream node. I opened a ticket to add circuit-breaker on the client.

priya: routing done. traffic shifted. latency down ~30% and 5xx volume decreasing. PD still firing because historical alert rule is naive (alerts on raw 5xx count).

olivia: customer-ops: opened support threads for the three customers who reported errors. will follow up post-incident and include refund recommendation if SLA hit.

sre-oncall-jamie: summary to include in post-incident: cause = downstream kvstore regression + connection pool exhaustion + noisy alert rule. immediate mitigations = routing fallback, rollback, PD dedupe/ratecap. Next: tune alerts and add dashboard for dedupe visibility.

matt: agree. let's plan after-action work: - change alert to be rate-per-1000-requests instead of absolute 5xx count - add grouping key on `service + region + error_type` - add a sliding dedupe window config in alert-manager (match PD routing) - create a 'signal-culler' dashboard to show alert storm metrics and grouped counts

priya: proposing new Prometheus rule idea (sketch):
```
- alert: InferenceHighErrorRate
  expr: sum(rate(inference_requests_total{code=~"5.."}[2m])) / sum(rate(inference_requests_total[2m])) > 0.03
  for: 3m
  labels:
    severity: page
  annotations:
    summary: "High 5xx rate on {{ $labels.instance }}"
```
This switches to relative rate and short `for` to avoid flapping.

olivia: also consider a rate-limited PD policy: at most 2 pages per 10m for the same grouping key, then escalate to a Slack-only channel for info. reduces oncall fatigue for noisy regressions.

sre-oncall-jamie: +1. we should also make PD grouping keys deterministic: `{{cluster}}:{{region}}:{{error_class}}` so incidents about the same root cause group together. currently alerts use instance id which fragments pages.

product-ops: make sure we map grouped incidents back to customers impacted in the summary — add a `impacted_customers` annotation pulling from recent support tickets? might be noisy but useful for triage.

matt: action items I'll take: add circuit-breaker client change (MR), instrument connection pool metrics, and add an initial dashboard panel for `conn_pool_wait_seconds`.

priya: action items I'll take: update alert rule prototype in staging, create routing toggles for fallback-model rollouts, and add a short playbook note for when to apply temporary routing.

olivia: action items I'll take: coordinate customer comms and draft post-incident note for the public incidents doc.

sre-oncall-jamie: squad-level changes: 1) Alert rule rewrite (owner: priya) 2) PD routing & ratecap config (owner: infra) 3) Grouping key standard (owner: matt) 4) Signal-culler dashboard (owner: jamie) — aim to complete in two sprints.

priya: quick question — for grouping heuristics do we prefer to add more labels to alerts (error_class) or use alertmanager routing with matchers? thinking alertmanager is more flexible for rate-limiting per-group.

matt: prefer alert labels + alertmanager routing. label once at source, route/rate-limit centrally. reduces duplication in rules.

infra-bot: created infra ticket INF-4321: add PD ratecap and standard grouping key. Link: https://infra/repo/INF-4321

sre-oncall-jamie: handoff — I'm going offline for the 2pm rotation. @matt will be on-call lead for the next 4 hours. please escalate to PD for customer-impact if error rate climbs back > 5% for more than 10m.

matt: ack, will monitor. feel free to ping me in the channel or escalate on PD.

olivia: closing notes: we did a good job with temporary routing + rollback. big takeaway: absolute-count alerts are fragile for multi-region traffic spikes. set of post-incident homework above — I'll pull together a confluence with timeline and attach dashboard links. :thumbsup:

sre-oncall-jamie: thanks team. I'll draft the postmortem template entries and link to INF-4321 and the alert MR once ready.

product-ops: adding one more: add a runbook snippet for 'apply temporary dedupe and route to fallback' under oncall playbooks so next person doesn't have to improvise.

matt: fine by me. closing thread once PRs are queued.

incident-bot: Incident closed — PD incident P1 resolved at 00:52 UTC. Metrics returning to normal.
